cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T4 answers T2's reintroduction plan; T5 builds on T4; T7 contests T6 directly.
cells.limitation: T9 skips T7's challenge to the Skeptic's motive reading and pivots to safety.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T4 adds residual sensitivity confounding retests; T5 turns it into a clean-baseline rule.
cells.limitation: T10 mostly recaps the plan rather than adding a new distinction.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T7-T8 examine diagnosis versus simply ending discomfort as competing aims.
cells.limitation: No turn considers active ingredients (acids, retinoids) or a shared ingredient across products.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T8 maps T6 and T7's readings onto different advice; T10 keeps one disagreement open.
cells.limitation: T9 concedes a safety point nobody disputed, a scripted rather than earned convergence.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D: calm first, then one change at a time, with the remaining dispute named.
cells.limitation: The open question on how much investigation is worth it stays at the T7 level.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T7 restates T6's attachment reading accurately before contesting it.
cells.limitation: T4 calls T2's plan a 'rush to retest' though T2 said 'once calm'.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T4 names the assumption of a recovered baseline and the innocent-product error; T5 answers.
cells.limitation: Nobody tests the forearm patch site or the few-days spacing proposed in T5 and T2.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T9's confounders (detergent, sun, wind, hot showers) are accurate and relevant.
cells.limitation: T5's forearm patch may miss facial irritation; T2's few-days gap may miss delayed reactions (suspected).

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: Section E separates severe signs from mild cases and admits products may not be the cause.
cells.limitation: T1 states 'your skin is already telling you it is overloaded' as fact.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T5 concedes T4 ('Fair') and narrows its claim to a clean-baseline test.
cells.limitation: The Skeptic never answers T7's objection to T6; T9 concedes an uncontested point instead.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern, including ambiguity about what the user is really asking
cells.example: Section A names severity and irritation versus allergy as the decisive unknowns.
cells.limitation: T6's motive reading is a stretch for a practical skin question, as T7 notes.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T8 uses 'three products' to show testing could rescue two of three.
cells.limitation: The one-week timing never informs whether this looks like irritation or delayed allergy.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: T7 grounds its reading in the user's literal question about finding the cause.
cells.limitation: T10's 'ones they would miss' is the speaker's preference, not a stated user priority.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: Section E sets red-flag symptoms where home testing stops and a clinician takes over.
cells.limitation: T6 invents 'hope and money' investment, though offered as a rejectable reading.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on severity, on fading after stopping, and on wanting comfort.
cells.limitation: Never asks which product types or ingredients, or whether stinging occurs only on application.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T6 offers rescue-the-routine and fear-of-damage as alternatives; Section D poses them as reflection.
cells.limitation: T6 phrases 'part of them wants a clean villain' close to an assertion.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T3 exposes the favorite-suspect assumption; Section E questions that products are the cause.
cells.limitation: The assumption that one product alone is responsible, not a combination, goes unexamined.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T8 and Section D contrast rescuing products with simply feeling comfortable.
cells.limitation: Cost and effort of the products versus weeks of testing is not weighed explicitly.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T6 names fear of lasting damage without pathologising.
cells.limitation: Fear appears in one line of T6 and is not developed afterward.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: T6 frames 'a reading the user can reject'; Section D leaves the choice with the user.
cells.limitation: Few distinctions are offered for the user to refine beyond the motive split.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options, including waiting, learning more, or a limited step
cells.example: Section E: clinician, slow reintroduction, drop all, or dermatologist if no easing.
cells.limitation: Reducing frequency of a likely active, a limited step, is not offered.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs in terms that matter to the user; no option treated as costless
cells.example: Section E weighs information value against re-irritation risk for the comfort-seeker.
cells.limitation: Time cost of a multi-week reintroduction is not stated.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: swelling, hives or spreading redness means clinician; mild and fading favours reintroduction.
cells.limitation: 'A week or two' threshold in Section E is not drawn from the user's facts.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section A flags severity as decisive; T9 separates confounders from product effects.
cells.limitation: Irritation versus allergy is named but not tied to how each changes the test.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps that follow from the analysis and fit the constraints
cells.example: T10 and Section E: pause, settle, reintroduce singly, keep dated notes.
cells.limitation: The cheapest step, comparing ingredient labels for a shared culprit, is never suggested.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T1 and T5 give plain, concrete instructions a layperson can follow.
cells.limitation: T2's 'could have been proven innocent, and wasn't' is slightly convoluted.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T7 'I'd contest that' clearly targets T6; T9 'the safety point' points to T8.
cells.limitation: T8 'those two readings' could mean T6's two motives or T6 versus T7.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Ten turns, all within word range, each carrying one move.
cells.limitation: The full plan is set by T2, leaving later turns refining it.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices, with explicit changes of position
cells.example: Subtractor, Experimenter and Skeptic hold clearly different roles throughout.
cells.limitation: Registers are similar; T10's Subtractor refers to Taleb in third person, blurring the voice.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Sections D and E consolidate rather than repeat turn text.
cells.limitation: T10 and Section E restate the same pause-then-reintroduce plan.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension arising from the issue itself
cells.example: T4 and T7 create real tension: retest risk and whether investigating is worth it.
cells.limitation: Stakes stay modest; the severity scenario is barely dramatised beyond T8.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals that stay plausible. ★ A reversal the text traces to an earlier turn's argument, naming what changed the speaker's mind. A change of position with no stated cause is a template, not a reversal
cells.example: T5 'Fair, and that sharpens my claim' traces its narrowing to T4.
cells.limitation: No real reversal; T9's concession answers no prior disagreement.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice without caricature
cells.example: T1's blunt 'fourth problem' and T3's 'embarrass your favorite suspect' show character.
cells.limitation: Personalities flatten into a shared measured register from T8 onward.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T3: 'designed to embarrass your favorite suspect, not flatter it.'
cells.limitation: Few analogies or images after T3; later turns are procedural.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement, with varied rhythm rather than constant intensity
cells.example: T6-T7 shift from procedure to the user's motives, varying the rhythm.
cells.limitation: Emotional movement is slight; T10 lands as a summary.

strengths: T4-T5 develop a real methodological distinction (clean baseline) that later shapes the plan.
Section E gives observable red-flag conditions that route to a clinician versus home testing.
T6-T8 turn a motive question into different advice, with T7 contesting rather than accepting it.
weaknesses: No mind raises ingredient types or a shared ingredient across the three products, the obvious first lead.
The Skeptic never answers T7's objection; T9 concedes an uncontested safety point instead.
T5's forearm patch and T2's few-days spacing go unchallenged despite likely limits for facial irritation.

symptoms.observed: No turn considers which ingredients or actives might cause stinging, or shared ingredients.
symptoms.evidence: likely the one with the strongest-sounding ingredient

symptoms.observed: Skeptic never responds to T7's challenge; concedes an undisputed point instead.
symptoms.evidence: I'll concede the safety point, and add a limit

symptoms.observed: Next steps skip the cheap label comparison before weeks of reintroduction.
symptoms.evidence: bring products back singly and keep a simple note

symptoms.observed: Forearm patch test proposed for facial stinging without noting its limits.
symptoms.evidence: small spot like the inner forearm or behind the ear

symptoms.observed: Never asks whether stinging happens only on application or persists all day.
symptoms.evidence: Whether the stinging is mild or severe

findings.description: Forearm or behind-ear patch tests may not reproduce irritant stinging on thinner facial skin; limitation unstated.
Reintroducing products a few days apart may be too short to catch delayed allergic reactions.
Mind-to-book bases (Popper, Kahneman, Taleb) are paraphrased in spirit; no quotations, nothing checkable.
The Taleb-based Subtractor refers to Taleb in third person, blurring the mind's identity.

rubric_fit_notes: A practical medical troubleshooting question fits criterion 4 loosely; motive speculation (T6) sits partly outside what the user asked. The ungrounded_number entry refers to Section E's 'a week or two', which has no turn number.
raw.question_type_note: Read as a troubleshooting decision: cells were scored on choosing between stopping, testing, dropping products, or seeing a clinician.
